title: Counting a Repayment Plan from the Determination Date — Benefit Overpayment Accounts Training Bulletin
content:
A new repayment plan on Benefit Overpayment Accounts set well after the determination is counted from the determination date: months are taken off the plan months according to the whole months elapsed from the determination date to the handling date.

| Whole months elapsed from the determination date to the handling date | Months taken off the plan months |
|---|---|
| More than 6 (the full-anchor months) | All of those whole months |
| At least 3 (the partial-anchor months) and no more than 6 | Those whole months less one |
| Fewer than 3 | None |

## Questions answered

**What does "counted from the determination date" mean for a plan set seven months after the determination?** All seven whole months are taken off the plan months, as if the plan had started at the determination.

**And for a plan set four months after?** Three months are taken off: four whole months less one.

**And for a plan set within two months?** Nothing is taken off; the plan is counted from the day it is set.

## Table of every case up to eight months

| Whole months elapsed | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Months taken off | 0 | 0 | 0 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 7 | 8 |

At exactly 6 whole months five months are taken off, and at 7 whole months all seven are.
